subject: math.AC
name: Zariski–Lipman conjecture
statement: If X is a normal variety over a field of characteristic zero and its tangent sheaf Der(O_X) is locally free, must X be smooth?
importance: Tests whether a fundamental infinitesimal invariant detects all algebraic singularities.
status_note: Known for several classes of singularities, including log canonical varieties; the unrestricted normal characteristic-zero case remains open.

references.title: Bongiorno, Regular Leaves of Singular Foliations

subject: math.AC
name: Auslander–Reiten conjecture for commutative local rings
statement: For a commutative Noetherian local ring R and a finitely generated R-module M, does Ext_R^i(M,M ⊕ R)=0 for every i>0 imply that M is free?
importance: Connects vanishing of self-extensions with projectivity and the structure of local rings.
status_note: Many complete-intersection and other special cases are known; no assumption here restricts R to those cases.

references.title: Lyle, On the totally acyclic condition and the Auslander–Reiten Conjecture

subject: math.AC
name: Huneke–Wiegand problem for complete-intersection domains
statement: Let R be a one-dimensional Noetherian local complete-intersection domain and M a nonzero finitely generated torsion-free R-module. If M ⊗_R Hom_R(M,R) is torsion-free, must M be free?
importance: Asks whether tensor products detect nontrivial modules over complete intersections.
status_note: The hypersurface case is proved. This entry asks about higher codimension complete intersections; the broader Gorenstein conjecture has a reported 2026 counterexample.

references.title: Celikbas, Le, Matsui and Sadeghi, Remarks on a conjecture of Huneke and Wiegand and the vanishing of (co)homology
A Counterexample to the Huneke–Wiegand Conjecture (general Gorenstein version)

subject: math.AC
name: Lech multiplicity conjecture
statement: For every flat local homomorphism (R,m) → (S,n) of Noetherian local rings, is the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity inequality e_m(R) ≤ e_n(S) valid?
importance: Would give a basic numerical monotonicity law for flat families of singularities.
status_note: Proved in low dimensions and for several graded situations; the general high-dimensional case remains open.

references.title: Ma, Lim Ulrich sequences and Lech’s conjecture

subject: math.AC
name: Buchsbaum–Eisenbud–Horrocks Betti-number conjecture
statement: If R is a regular local ring of dimension d and M is a nonzero finite-length R-module, does the minimal free resolution satisfy β_i^R(M) ≥ binomial(d,i) for every 0 ≤ i ≤ d?
importance: Predicts the smallest possible individual syzygy sizes for modules supported at a point.
status_note: The total-rank bound is known in broad settings; that does not establish these separate bounds on every Betti number. This is the module version, not a false extension to arbitrary complexes.

references.title: VandeBogert and Walker, The Total Rank Conjecture in Characteristic Two

subject: math.AC
name: Eisenbud–Green–Harris conjecture
statement: Let I ⊂ k[x_1,...,x_n] be homogeneous and contain a regular sequence of degrees a_1 ≤ ... ≤ a_n. Must there be a homogeneous ideal J containing x_1^{a_1},...,x_n^{a_n} with the same Hilbert function as I?
importance: Would extend Macaulay’s Hilbert-function theory to ideals containing a prescribed complete intersection.
status_note: Known for a number of degree sequences and small-variable cases; the arbitrary degree-sequence statement is open.

references.title: Caviglia, De Stefani and Sbarra, The Eisenbud–Green–Harris Conjecture

subject: math.AC
name: Eisenbud–Goto bound for smooth varieties
statement: For a smooth irreducible nondegenerate projective variety X ⊂ P^r over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, is reg(I_X) ≤ deg(X) − codim(X) + 1?
importance: Would sharply control defining equations and syzygies using elementary geometric data.
status_note: The original conjecture for arbitrary varieties is false. Only the smooth characteristic-zero restriction is asked here; curves and many smooth special cases are known.

references.title: Kwak and Park, A bound for Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity by double point divisors

subject: math.AC
name: Small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture in positive characteristic
statement: Does every complete Noetherian local domain R of characteristic p>0 admit a nonzero finitely generated R-module M with depth_R(M)=dim(R)?
importance: Seeks finite modules that remove the homological defects of arbitrary local singularities.
status_note: Big Cohen–Macaulay modules and algebras are known, but their existence does not supply a finite module. This entry does not assert the false graded characteristic-zero refinement.

references.title: Shimomoto and Tavanfar, Remarks on the Small Cohen–Macaulay conjecture and new instances of maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules

subject: math.AC
name: Harbourne–Huneke containment for arbitrary point sets
statement: For the radical homogeneous ideal I of any nonempty finite set of points in P^N over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with irrelevant ideal m, is I^{(Nr)} ⊆ m^{r(N−1)} I^r for every integer r≥1?
importance: Would strengthen the central comparison between symbolic and ordinary powers of point ideals.
status_note: Recent results establish the containment for general point configurations; this question includes all finite configurations, not only general ones.

references.title: Malara, From Demailly’s Inequality to Harbourne–Huneke Containments for General Points

subject: math.AC
name: Nagata conjecture for nonsquare numbers of points
statement: Let r≥10 be nonsquare and let p_1,...,p_r be very general points of P^2_C. Must every nonzero homogeneous polynomial vanishing to order at least m at each p_i have degree d ≥ m√r?
importance: Gives a fundamental lower bound for fat-point interpolation and asymptotic symbolic-power growth.
status_note: Nagata proved the square-number case. The stated nonsquare cases remain open; very general positions are essential.
